page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and utilizes the Xen hypervisor. It is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB of RAM per physical core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while network performance is anchored by a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor and memory subsystems operate in lower performance tiers compared to modern hardware. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10% category. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor throughput, with uncached large-block reads registering at 22.62 GB/sec and writes at 14.23 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations, supported by hardware-accelerated instructions like AES and AVX, show weak performance in Passmark tests. Redis SET operations reach 2.54 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 2.81 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i3.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require high-capacity, low-latency local storage without demanding high CPU compute power. However, the tradeoff is its lower-tier CPU and memory performance. This instance is best suited for storage-intensive workloads, local database hosting, caching layers like Redis, and basic web serving where local storage capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
